Subject: POC: network fencing & air-gap options — post-call actions

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and next steps from our side. Appreciate you walking us through the MediqCare constraints and PHI flows.

Key takeaways: 
- POC scope: private inference for clinical notes (PHI) with optional air-gapped on-prem for gold-standard isolation.
- Primary ask: confirm current network topology, VLANs/CIDR ranges, where PHI originates and whether any third-party integrations will require egress.
- Compliance: MediqCare asked about SOC 2 and HIPAA agreements and whether Redwood can provide BAA + evidence artifacts.

Requested from MediqCare (could you send by EOD Tue):
1) current network diagram (LAN/VPC, CIDRs, firewalls)
2) completed vendor security questionnaire (we can start with the spreadsheet you mentioned)
3) brief list of PHI flows (systems involved, egress destinations, expected throughput)

What we’ll do next (Redwood):
- Jonas will propose two topology options for the POC: a) VPC-isolated, tenant-dedicated design with strict egress controls, b) air-gapped on-prem appliance flow for offline-only inference.
- Rishi will confirm BAAs and what evidence we can provide up front (SOC 2 artifacts, encryption, logging retention).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week to walk the MediqCare infra team through the diagrams and answer network-specific questions.

Attachments: none in this message — please send your diagram and questionnaire.

Proposed times for the tech deep-dive (please pick one): Tue 11/7 09:00-09:30 PT, Tue 11/7 15:30-16:00 PT, Wed 11/8 10:00-10:30 PT.

Thanks — Olga

A few quick clarifications: 
- We consider PHI to be clinical notes + attachments. Inbound from our EHR (Cerner) and some lab systems; no external analytics vendors currently.
- For the POC we prefer to start with private VPC + strict egress; air-gap is desirable but may be scoped later depending on timeline/cost. Can Redwood support a fully air-gapped on-prem appliance for the full inference stack, or only a gated data transfer model?
- SOC 2 status and HIPAA — can you share whether Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and whether you have a standard BAA? Our security team wants to see where Redwood stands before the tech deep-dive.

Available for the deep-dive: Tue 11/7 15:30 PT works for our infra lead.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: POC: network fencing & air-gap options — post-call actions

Quick technical read: reviewed mediqcare-network-diagram.pdf. High-level notes below — I'll publish a short PDF draft (redwood-topology-options-draft.pdf) for the call.

High-level options for POC:
1) VPC-dedicated (recommended first step)
   - Dedicated tenant in our hosted fleet, private VPC with VPC peering to MediqCare's VPC.
   - Private subnets for inference nodes, NAT disabled for worker nodes; egress only via controlled bounces through a customer-managed proxy or an approved egress appliance.
   - Required from MediqCare: CIDR ranges, inbound NACLs, port openings (SSH for maintenance disabled; only TLS endpoints allowed from specific IPs), and a small set of public egress IPs if pulling model updates.

2) Full air-gapped on-prem appliance (higher effort, full isolation)
   - We can deploy an appliance image that runs inference locally. Updates are delivered via signed bundles you pull into an isolated RPM/OCI repo (offline process).
   - Constraints: no KV cache sharing, longer model update windows, and we need a secure transfer procedure for artifacts. Also needs an approved maintenance window and out-of-band attestation for software integrity.

Artifacts to prepare for MediqCare pre-call:
- redwood-topology-options-draft.pdf (attached) — proposed diagrams and a pros/cons matrix
- list of required network artifacts: CIDRs, firewall rules, expected throughput, SFTP/rsync endpoints for airgap
- suggested test plan for the POC (sample dataset, throughput targets, acceptance criteria)

I'll attach the draft topology and share the short notes internally. For the deep-dive I recommend Jonas + infra engineer (I can bring Samir on Redwood side if needed).

Jonas Weber
Principal Systems Architect | Redwood Inference
